01_overview.title: The window
01_overview.summary: Mule has four modes: Draw puts lines down, Edit changes them, Notes holds prompts for the AI, Shots shows timing. Any question about Mule: give the file AI_HANDBOOK.md to your AI and ask it.
legend: Modes Draw · Edit · Notes · Shots (Tab, N), display buttons on the right
Tools of the current mode (pen, brush, eraser …)
Viewport: Alt or Space + mouse buttons move the camera
Outliner: planes, stroke objects, surfaces, nulls
Status line: what is active and which keys work right now

02_pen_brush.title: Pen and brush – both draw lines
02_pen_brush.summary: Pen and brush both draw lines you can edit and build surfaces from. The only difference is the look: the pen draws grey pencil, the brush draws in the current colour.
legend: Pen (A): grey pencil line for construction – never coloured
Brush (A again): the same kind of line, in colour with a brush texture
The current colour (click: colour wheel) – it is the brush colour
Both are real lines: select, snap, fill, loft, extrude

03_paint_mode.title: Draw mode and Paint mode
03_paint_mode.summary: In Draw mode pen and brush make lines – the construction. In Paint mode they lay colour flat onto the surface – for look and shading, never for the shape.
steps: Draw mode · lines
Paint mode (S) · paint
Edit · select everything
legend: Paint mode (S): pen and brush lay down paint instead of lines
Lines: editable – they snap, weld and build surfaces
Paint: flat on the surface, like colour – not selectable, only the eraser cuts it
Paint follows its surface (lofts, fill surfaces); S again: back to lines

04_free_mode.title: Free mode (Q) – drawing without a plane
04_free_mode.summary: Free mode draws in space without a plane: the stroke lies in an imagined plane through its start point, facing the camera. It must start on an existing line or surface; its end may dock somewhere else.
steps: Step 1 · start on a line
Step 2 · the end docks to another line
legend: Free (Q): button in the left bar – a green frame shows it is on
Start the stroke on a line or a surface – never in empty space
The end docks to a point or line at any depth
For connections, arcs and frames between things you already drew

05_hold_shape.title: Straight lines and shapes: hold still
05_hold_shape.summary: Draw freely; if you hold still for a moment at the end of a stroke, Mule turns it into a straight line or a clean shape.
steps: Step 1 · draw roughly
Step 2 · hold still at the end
legend: Keep the pointer still for a moment at the end: the stroke becomes a clean shape
Recognised: straight line, circle, rectangle, arc
Until you release, the mouse adjusts size or end point; Ctrl: square
Straight lines snap their angle in steps

06_new_plane.title: Own planes: Space+N
06_new_plane.summary: You always draw onto a plane or surface. Space+N creates a new plane exactly where the cursor points – for example at the handle of the cup – so you can draw details there.
steps: Step 1 · point at the handle, Space+N
Step 2 · orbit: the plane stands in space
Step 3 · draw on it
legend: Point at a line or surface and press Space+N: a new plane through that point
The plane faces the camera; orbit to see where it stands in space
Draw on it like on paper; wheel or [ ]: move it along its normal
X / Y / Z: back to a ground plane; click a plane to make it the target

07_draw_on_surface.title: Drawing on surfaces: lines shape, paint colours
07_draw_on_surface.summary: You can draw directly on surfaces and meshes. Lines drawn on a surface become its control lines and shape it; paint only colours it.
steps: Step 1 · click a surface: you draw on it
Step 2 · draw a line across it
Step 3 · move a point of the line
Paint mode (S) · colour the surface
legend: Click a surface, plane or mesh: it becomes the target (status line: Drawing on …)
Pen or brush draws on it; a line from border to border becomes a control line of the surface
Move the line or its points (Edit, point mode): the surface follows its lines
Paint mode (S): colour lies flat on the surface – look and shading, never the shape
Lines build the form, paint decorates it

08_edit_gizmo.title: Edit mode (Tab): select and transform
08_edit_gizmo.summary: Tab switches to Edit mode. Select what you want to change, then T, R or E shows the gizmo to move, rotate or scale it.
legend: Move (T)
Rotate (R)
Scale (E) – past the pivot: mirror
The gizmo sits on the selection: drag an arrow, ring or square
Click selects, Shift adds, Ctrl removes; Ctrl while dragging snaps
Points (1) · edges (2) · surfaces (3) choose what you select

09_extrude.title: Extrude (X)
09_extrude.summary: Extruding pulls a copy of the selected lines away and builds walls between them – the quickest way from a drawn outline to a volume.
steps: Step 1 · select the lines
Step 2 · press X, move the mouse
legend: Edit mode (Tab), edge mode (key 2)
Select the lines – click, Shift adds, L: connected
Press X, move the mouse: that sets the length
The copy follows; walls appear between the lines
Status line: X/Y/Z axis · N normal · Ctrl snaps · click confirms · Esc cancels

10_loft.title: Loft (Shift+F)
10_loft.summary: A loft is a curved surface through several cross-sections, like Skin in Houdini: draw the sections, select them in order, press Shift+F.
steps: Step 1 · select the cross-sections in order
Step 2 · Shift+F
legend: Edit mode, edge mode: click the cross-sections one after another
The click order is the order of the loft
Shift+F: a curved surface through all of them (Ctrl+Shift+F: ring back to the first)
Closed sections give a tube, open ones a sheet; the surface follows its lines

11_fill.title: Surface from lines (F)
11_fill.summary: Surfaces always come from lines: select lines that close an outline and press F.
steps: Step 1 · select the outline
Step 2 · F
legend: Edit mode, edge mode: select lines that close an outline (L selects connected lines)
F builds a curve surface; an outline bent inwards becomes a fill surface
The surface follows its lines: move the lines, the surface moves along
Alt+F forces a smooth curve surface from curved border lines

12_insert_point.title: Insert a point (Ctrl+click)
12_insert_point.summary: Points are where you can grab a line. Ctrl+click on a line adds a point exactly there.
steps: Step 1 · point mode (key 1)
Step 2 · Ctrl+click on the line
legend: Edit mode, point mode (key 1): line ends and corners show as points
Ctrl+click on a line: a new point there, selected – drag it to reshape the line
Ctrl+click on a point deselects it; hold S and drag: slide points along their line

13_delete_point.title: Delete points (point mode)
13_delete_point.summary: Three ways to get rid of a point: dissolve it and keep the shape, remove it and smooth the line, or delete it together with its pieces.
steps: Selected point
Del · dissolve
Ctrl+Del · delete
legend: Select a point (point mode, key 1)
Del dissolves: the point is gone, the line keeps its shape
Shift+Del removes: the line runs smoothly between the neighbours
Ctrl+Del deletes: the pieces go, a straight line bridges the neighbours

14_symmetry.title: Groups and generators: Symmetry
14_symmetry.summary: Generators work like in Cinema 4D: put objects under a Symmetry or Array null and Mule shows the copies live.
legend: Objects → Symmetry: a generator null; the selected objects go under it
Draw one half – the other half appears live and updates while you draw
Alt+G: plain group (null); Objects → Array: copies on a circle, line or path
Alt+C (Convert): turns the generator into real lines

15_note_board.title: Notes (N) and the note board
15_note_board.summary: Notes are prompts in space: a short heading points at a part, and its board holds everything the AI should know about it. The octopus says which similar parts the same note also means.
steps: Step 1 · Notes mode (N): double-click on a part
Step 2 · camera button: the view goes onto the board
Step 3 · write into the board
Step 4 · octopus: the note also means similar parts
legend: Double-click in Notes mode: a note with a leader line to that part
Camera button at the note: a picture of the view goes onto its board
Bottom right: the board of the active note – pictures, videos, arrows
Type, paste or drop pictures into it; it is what the AI reads about this part
Octopus: Shift+drag from the anchor (or right-click → add selection) – the note means these too

16_hero_camera.title: Hero camera
16_hero_camera.summary: Hero cameras are the views that matter most. Tick a screenshot on a note board as hero camera, and the AI looks through exactly this camera while it builds and reviews.
steps: Step 1 · click the screenshot: the check box appears
Step 2 · ticked: name it – turquoise frame
legend: Tick “hero camera” at the top right of a screenshot on the board
Give the camera a name (default Hero 1, Hero 2 …)
A turquoise frame marks hero pictures
The brief renders a clean picture and a USD camera from it
Without hero cameras the brief uses three standard angles

17_brief_dialog.title: Export Sketch Brief (Ctrl+E)
17_brief_dialog.summary: The Sketch Brief is the hand-over to the AI: a folder with pictures, notes, the scene as USD and working rules. The dialog asks only for what the AI cannot read from the scene.
legend: The task in one sentence
Hints that apply only to this export
Discuss only – nothing gets built
Brief recipe: the way of working – Mule Default or your own (…)
Autoprompt: a ready sentence for the AI chat lands on the clipboard
Then choose a folder; start Claude Code or Codex in that brief folder

18_review_mark.title: Review: talk your feedback
18_review_mark.summary: Walk through the scene and talk, like in a review session. Mule records your voice and where you looked and pointed; the AI turns it into draft notes.
legend: While recording, a click sets a numbered marker exactly there
Mark tool (on at the start) – off: work normally, the recording goes on
Review → Start Review: voice, camera and pointer are recorded
Send Review: transcribes and puts a sentence on the clipboard
Paste it into the AI chat yourself (Ctrl+V) – nothing is sent automatically
The AI then writes draft notes at the marked parts; you accept them

19_shots.title: Shots: what happens when
19_shots.summary: Shots shows timing without animating: drawings per frame on flipbook layers, camera positions and notes about what happens between them.
steps: Step 1 · Space+N: flipbook layer, draw at frame 1001
Step 2 · frame 1012: draw the next state
Step 3 · shot note with camera: what happens in between
legend: Timeline: one row per flipbook layer; a drawing holds until the next one
Shots panel: shot notes with text and camera positions
Space+N in Shots: a flipbook layer; draw at any frame, O: onion skin
Nothing is animated – the notes say what happens in between
